paragraph: In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Angola among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). The stations come under the EU-funded ClimSA programme, through a contract with Tecnavia signed in November 2023. A 2019 to 2022 modernisation of the weather service INAMET had [included a system to receive the EUMETCast data stream](<https://www.mfi.fr/turnkey-projects/pmi-project-global-modernization-project/>). In the last twelve months, the Commission's May 2026 list recorded the station installed. No source found since October 2023 says INAMET uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

Burundi's weather institute IGEBU [runs a satellite imagery viewer](<https://www.igebu.bi/data-tools/>) on its site, showing Meteosat Second Generation layers such as precipitation rate and convection. In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Burundi among eight member states [still waiting for a PUMA station](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>), under a continental contract signed in November 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says IGEBU uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

[In September 2024 the government said a new PUMA station would be installed in Benin to process Meteosat Third Generation data](<https://www.gouv.bj/article/2777/meteo-benin-renforce-systeme-satellitaire-travers-eumetsat/>). [The installation was set for the 16th EUMETSAT User Forum in Cotonou, 16 to 20 September 2024](<https://www.gouv.bj/article/2777/meteo-benin-renforce-systeme-satellitaire-travers-eumetsat/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In August 2025 the national meteorology agency ANAM [said its new PUMA 2025 station](<https://meteoburkina.bf/news/lanam-poursuit-la-modernisation-de-ses-infrastructures-des-stations-de-derni%C3%A8re-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ration-pour-mieux-servir-le-burkina-faso/>) receives Meteosat Third Generation data every ten minutes. ANAM says the ten-minute data [help it issue more responsive early alerts](<https://meteoburkina.bf/news/lanam-poursuit-la-modernisation-de-ses-infrastructures-des-stations-de-derni%C3%A8re-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ration-pour-mieux-servir-le-burkina-faso/>). A 2025 ANAM presentation says the agency [obtained ISO 9001:2015 certification](<https://climateservices.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/2_SLAPIS_Coop-et-Meteo-Sawadogo.pdf>) that year. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Burkina Faso. Nothing found says which services the certification covers.

In December 2023 China [donated a P31 million transportable satellite ground system](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/76992>) to the Department of Meteorological Services, the government's Daily News reported. A memorandum between the two governments was still to be signed. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Botswana, among 41 member states. Nothing found says the donated station is installed or receiving. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

No stage is set. [In August 2025 ASECNA's aeronautical information publication listed METEOSAT (MSG) satellite images among the equipment of the Bangui/M'Poko Centre Meteorologique Principal](<https://aim.asecna.aero/html/eAIP/FR-_04AD-2.FEFF-fr-FR.html>), an airport centre. [The centre also offers satellite imagery on request in flight documentation](<https://aim.asecna.aero/html/eAIP/FR-_04AD-2.FEFF-fr-FR.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the national weather service itself receives satellite data. Preparing would need the national meteorological service to have a satellite receiving station or data stream installed, contracted or being upgraded.

Daouda Konaté, director of the national meteorology service, [says Meteosat data let its forecasters issue nowcasts](<https://www.preventionweb.net/news/towards-early-warnings-all-africa>), which underpin the country's early warning platforms. He spoke to EUMETSAT in 2024. He says that when record rainfall was forecast for Abidjan in June 2024, [an orange alert was issued at once](<https://www.preventionweb.net/news/towards-early-warnings-all-africa>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service holds ISO 9001 certification. Mature would need the national meteorological service to hold ISO 9001 certification for its services.

Cameroon's national meteorological service [describes access to EUMETSAT nowcasting products](<https://meteocameroon.gov.cm/en/nwcsaf/>) on its own site, covering the next six hours. On 22 July 2025 its National Meteorological Directorate [began installing a PUMA-2025 reception station](<https://www.techreviewafrica.com/news/2530/cameroon-takes-major-leap-in-weather-forecasting-with-puma-2025-station-installation>), TechReviewAfrica reported. The station receives Meteosat Third Generation data every ten minutes. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

[In February 2024 a METTELSAT document hosted by WMO said the agency has PUMA 2015 and MESSIR NEO equipment](<https://wmo.int/sites/default/files/2024-02/4.%20Syst%C3%A8me%20d%E2%80%99Observation%20de%20la%20METTELSAT.pdf>), connected to the EUMETCast Africa data stream. [In July 2024 a MeteoSwiss peer review said METTELSAT's PUMA reception system at its headquarters is functional](<https://meteordcongo.cd/documents/14/DRC-CHD-Report-NGA-Annex_2.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Congo among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). Brazzaville had an earlier one: in September 2004 [a PUMA station for Meteosat Second Generation data was inaugurated](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2020-04/pdf_conf_6auf_report_en.pdf>) at Maya-Maya airport. In the last twelve months, the Commission's May 2026 list recorded the station installed. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In 2019 the Comoros meteorological service said it [received the EUMETCast stream through Synergie and PUMA stations](<https://severeweather.wmo.int/TCFW/RAI_Training2019/Comoros.pdf>). The agency ANACM said it [issued cyclone, heavy rain and flood warnings using that stream](<https://severeweather.wmo.int/TCFW/RAI_Training2019/Comoros.pdf>), but nothing since repeats it. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Comoros. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether the national weather service in Cape Verde receives or uses satellite data, so no station, data stream or use in forecasts is on record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source showing that the national meteorological service has a satellite receiving station or data stream installed, contracted or being upgraded.

A 2025 GeoSphere Austria peer review says Djibouti's meteorological agency [has no nowcasting observations other than web satellite imagery](<https://alliancehydromet.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Djibouti-CHD.pdf>). Its PUMA satellite workstation was not working, so imagery came through the web. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Djibouti. A 2022 World Bank roadmap had found [the Meteosat receiving station out of service](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099061323094013108/pdf/P1705480165e750370a40903df6490528c1.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

[On 23 March 2026 Boualem Sayah of the Office National de la Météorologie said](<https://algeriezoom.com/algerie-l-onm-muscle-ses-moyens-pour-des-previsions-meteo-plus-precises/>) Algeria exchanges millions of data a day with the WMO network, among them data from new-generation satellites that make the office's numerical models finer. [In April 2026 the office announced the renewal of its ISO 9001:2015 certification](<https://www.almasdar-dz.com/178184-%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%86-%D8%AA%D8%AC%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%AA%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%AF-%D8%B4%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%8A%D8%B2%D9%88-9001-2015-%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%B4%D8%B1-%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8A>). In the last twelve months, both statements date from 2026. No source found since November 2023 says the office's warnings draw on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

In September 2026 the head of forecasting and early warning at the Egyptian Meteorological Authority described [satellites as a key part of its observation system](<https://www.egyptke.com/293734>). He said the authority [has run an early warning system since 2020](<https://www.egyptke.com/293734>) that combines observations, satellites among them, with eight global numerical models. The Ministry of Civil Aviation's review of 2025 says the authority [renewed its ISO 9001:2015 certification](<https://www.civilaviation.gov.eg/Media/NewsDetails?NewsID=1620&title=%D8%AD%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%AF+%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%A6%D8%A9+%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%A9+%D9%84%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%B1%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%AF+%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%A9+%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D9%88%D9%8A%D8%A9+%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%85+2025>) that year. In the last twelve months, the September 2026 account is the latest statement. Nothing found shows how far satellite data shapes each warning.

In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Eritrea among eight member states [still waiting for a PUMA station](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). A contract with Tecnavia signed in November 2023 covers all 49 member states. In the last twelve months, the Commission's list recorded Eritrea's station as contracted and not yet installed, with no date of arrival. No national source found describes satellite data at the weather service. Nothing found says the station has been installed or that the service uses satellite data. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

The Ethiopian Meteorological Institute [publishes Meteosat imagery on its site](<https://www.ethiomet.gov.et/satellite-imagery/>), including precipitation rate, dust and a nowcasting product. The page also carries [a convection warning product for rapidly developing thunderstorms](<https://www.ethiomet.gov.et/satellite-imagery/>), made with EUMETSAT's NWC-SAF nowcasting software and read in August 2026. In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Ethiopia among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service holds ISO 9001 certification. Mature would need the national meteorological service to hold ISO 9001 certification for its services.

No stage is set. Nothing found since October 2023 says whether the national weather service in Gabon receives or uses satellite data, so no station, data stream or use in forecasts is on record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a source showing that the national meteorological service has a satellite receiving station or data stream installed, contracted or being upgraded.

In March 2025 the Ghana Meteorological Agency [received ISO 9001 re-certification](<https://gna.org.gh/2025/03/gmet-receives-international-organization-for-standardization-re-certification/>), the Ghana News Agency reported. A 2022 paper described [satellite nowcasting in use at the agency](<https://doi.org/10.22541/au.165712587.76658353/v1>). In the last twelve months, in November 2025 the agency [received PUMA-2025 and ClimSA stations](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/3202/ghana-meteorological-agency-enhances-forecasting-capabilities-with-new-eu-funded-climsa-systems>) that give Meteosat Third Generation images every ten minutes. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

Guinea's meteorological agency [publishes Meteosat products on its site](<https://anmeteo.gov.gn/imagerie-satellitaire/>), among them dust RGB, precipitation maps and a thunderstorm nowcasting product. The page is undated and was read in 2026. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Guinea. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

At a handover on 30 August 2024 the meteorology unit of the Department of Water Resources [received Meteosat Third Generation PUMA and ClimSA stations](<https://meteogambia.gm/news/department-of-water-resources-of-the-gambia-receives-advanced-meteosat-third-generation-puma-and-climsa-stations/>). They were installed with EU funds through the African Union Commission. In May 2026 the Commission listed Gambia among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says the unit's forecasts use the data. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Guinea-Bissau among eight member states [still waiting for a PUMA station](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the national meteorology institute INM-GB [completed installing a ClimSA and PUMA2025 station](<https://meteoguinebissau.gw/noticias/nova-esta%C3%A7%C3%A3o-climsa-e-puma2025/>) on 21 to 25 August 2026. It says the station was tested and accepted, and receives Meteosat Third Generation data in near real time. Nothing found says forecasts use the data. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In August 2024 the Kenya Meteorological Department says [the African Union Commission installed PUMA 2025 and ClimSA stations](<https://meteo.go.ke/news/puma-and-climsa-stations-tot-workshop/>) at its offices to capture Meteosat Third Generation data. EUMETSAT says the [Nairobi station was the first PUMA-2025 receiver](<https://www.meteorologicaltechnologyinternational.com/news/satellites/eumetsat-installs-receiving-stations-for-kenyas-meteosat-third-generation-geostationary-satellites.html>) installed in Africa. A November 2024 workshop trained staff to use the stations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the department uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

On 24 October 2025 the Liberia Meteorological Service and Tecnavia [completed installing a ClimSA and PUMA2025 system](<https://meteoliberia.com/news/liberia-meteorological-service-lms-installs-climsapuma2025-meteosat-third-generation-system-at-the-robert-international-airport/>) at Roberts International Airport. Funded by the EU, it receives Meteosat Third Generation model data and high-resolution imagery. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Liberia. No source found since October 2023 says the service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

[The Libya National Meteorological Service said its assessment of the extreme rain of August 2024 rested on satellite images and numerical models](<https://wmo.int/media/news-from-members/parts-of-libya-affected-extreme-weather-lnmc>). [The National Meteorological Centre said it issued early warnings 48 and 72 hours ahead of the two August 2024 episodes](<https://wmo.int/media/news-from-members/parts-of-libya-affected-extreme-weather-lnmc>), and sent them to public sectors and the media. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service holds ISO 9001 certification. Mature would need the national meteorological service to hold ISO 9001 certification for its services.

In 2023 a consultancy [deployed a nowcasting system](<https://wisconsultancy.com/projects/>) for the Lesotho Meteorological Service, combining observations, satellite data and model output. No later source says it still works. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Lesotho, among 41 member states. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In March 2025 a spokesman for Morocco's meteorology directorate DGM told SNRT News that it [bought third-generation satellite receivers](<https://snrtnews.com/article/117313>). The new equipment [lets the DGM issue accurate warning bulletins](<https://snrtnews.com/article/117313>). On 29 October 2025 the DGM [ordered a second follow-up audit](<https://tenderly.ma/marches-attribues/audit-de-suivi-n2-pour-le-maintien-de-la-certification-du-systeme-290704>) to keep its ISO 9001:2015 certification. In the last twelve months, the DGM said in December 2025 that [its observation draws on satellite images refreshed every ten minutes](<https://fr.le360.ma/societe/de-lobservation-aux-alertes-comment-la-dgm-prepare-ses-bulletins-meteo_74T4ZDGOOZEBTD4RQVUTJNIYPE/>). Nothing found shows which warnings draw on satellite data and which on radar or stations.

In 2019 the forecasting office [presented a recently upgraded PUMA 2015 station](<https://severeweather.wmo.int/TCFW/RAI_Training2019/Madagascar.pdf>) and said it used Meteosat imagery to follow tropical cyclones. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Madagascar, among 41 member states. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

On 10 March 2026 Mali-Meteo [commissioned PUMA 2025 and ClimSA equipment](<https://fr.apanews.net/disasters/mali-meteo-dotee-dun-systeme-satellitaire-de-nouvelle-generation/>), APAnews reported. It can now receive Meteosat Third Generation data in real time for its analysis and forecasts. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 also [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Mali. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

[In March 2025 WMO said Mozambique's warnings rest on forecasts using satellite imagery and surface observations](<https://wmo.int/site/science-action/weather-forecasts-and-early-warnings/mozambiques-life-saving-early-warning-systems>). [In September 2023 the World Bank said the national meteorology institute, INAM, used satellite images for warnings](<https://www.worldbank.org/pt/news/feature/2023/09/11/early-warning-system-saves-lives-in-afe-mozambique>), relayed through 70 community radios. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service holds ISO 9001 certification. Mature would need the national meteorological service to hold ISO 9001 certification for its services.

In September 2025 an African Union Commission committee [inspected the ClimSA and PUMA equipment installed in Nouakchott](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/pressreleases/45397-pr-Press_Release_Deployment_Final.pdf>), which receives and processes Meteosat Second and Third Generation data from EUMETSAT. In May 2026 the Commission listed Mauritania among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says the weather service's forecasts use the data. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In 2007 the Mauritius Meteorological Services [prepared cyclone warnings from satellite imagery](<https://metservice.intnet.mu/pdfs/technical-note-on-cyclone-season.pdf>). In the last twelve months, in September 2026 the acting director [listed MSG and MTG satellite imagery](<https://archive.uneca.org/archive2/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/CFND/RESIsland/Mauritius/mms_resisland.pdf>) among the service's working tools. The same deck dates the first satellite image reception to 1968. In May 2026 the African Union Commission listed Mauritius among 41 member states with [a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

In April 2025 the Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services said it uses the [Flash Flood Guidance System](<https://www.metmalawi.gov.mw/news/flash-flood-warnings-what-you-need-to-know-before-its-too-late/>), which combines satellite rainfall estimates with ground observations. The department says [its flash flood warnings are produced with tools](<https://www.metmalawi.gov.mw/news/flash-flood-warnings-what-you-need-to-know-before-its-too-late/>) that include that system. In August 2025 it [installed a PUMA 2025 reception system](<https://www.metmalawi.gov.mw/news/dccms-enhances-weather-monitoring-capabilities-with-climsa-satellite-system-upgrade/>) at its Blantyre headquarters. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's May 2026 list also [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>). No source found since October 2023 says the weather service holds ISO 9001 certification. Mature would need the national meteorological service to hold ISO 9001 certification for its services.

In July 2018 China [handed over FY-3 satellite data receiving and processing systems](<https://na.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/dsxx/hdjh/201807/t20180711_7709077.htm>) to the Namibia Meteorological Service. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Namibia, among 41 member states. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

Niger's meteorological directorate [runs a live satellite imagery page](<https://www.niger-meteo.ne/image-satelitaire/>) serving Meteosat products, among them precipitation rates and dust-storm imagery. A service displaying satellite products is taken to use them in its work. In the last twelve months, the African Union Commission's list of May 2026 [recorded a PUMA station installed](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/7-%20Infrastructure%20and%20Capacity%20Building_AUC_PDF.pdf>) in Niger. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service issues warnings drawing on satellite data. Operating would need the national meteorological service to issue early warnings or impact-based forecasts that draw on satellite data.

[NiMet said it completed installation of a PUMA 2025 / ClimSA Meteosat Third Generation receiving station at its headquarters on 9 May 2025](<https://nimet.gov.ng/news?id=123>). [It replaced the earlier MSG 2015 station](<https://nimet.gov.ng/news?id=123>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found since October 2023 says the weather service uses satellite data in its forecasts. Establishing would need the national meteorological service to use satellite data in its forecasts or nowcasting.

In May 2026 Meteo Rwanda [said it runs PUMA-2025 reception stations](<https://www-cdn.eumetsat.int/files/2026-05/9%20-RWANDA_MTG_and_Radar_Synergy_PDF.pdf>) that process and display Meteosat Third Generation data in real time.
